subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Maillard Reaction
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Maillard Reaction.

hook.text: The Maillard reaction is why bread browns, steak sears, and coffee develops its rich, complex flavors.

buildup.text: When amino acids and sugars are heated together above 140°C, they form hundreds of new flavor molecules.

discovery.text: In coffee, the Maillard reaction creates melanoidins—brown polymers responsible for body, color, and that roasty aroma.

twist.text: The reaction is non-enzymatic—it happens purely from heat. No living process is required, just temperature and time.

climax.text: Over 1,000 volatile compounds are created during coffee roasting. Most come from the Maillard reaction alone.

punchline.text: Sugars plus amino acids plus heat. One reaction creates a thousand flavors.

quiz.question: What does the Maillard reaction create in coffee?
options: Melanoidins—brown polymers for body, color, and roasty aroma
